items.summary: Hurricane Simon reached Category 4 with 145 mph (230 kph) winds on Sunday, Oct 11, sitting about 65 miles WNW of Manzanillo with a hurricane warning in effect along Mexico's west-central coast. President Claudia Sheinbaum urged residents of Jalisco, Colima, Nayarit and Michoacán to shelter indoors; evacuations were ongoing. Mexico's civil protection agency placed 28 municipalities in Jalisco and Colima at the highest cyclone alert level and 93 more at high alert. Puerto Vallarta's international airport temporarily closed Sunday; Jalisco suspended classes in 22 coastal municipalities.
items.title: Oct 11: Hurricane Simon at Category 4 (145 mph) nears Mexico's west-central coast; evacuations and warnings

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (06:00 UTC advisory)
items.summary: As of the 06:00 UTC Monday advisory, Simon had weakened to Category 3 with 115 mph (185 km/h) winds, centered near 19.9N 106.2W — about 140 miles WNW of Manzanillo and 45 miles SW of Cabo Corrientes — moving NW at 5 mph; whether the center would cross inland or stay just offshore was still uncertain. NHC forecast an additional 2-4 inches (5-10 cm) of rain through early Thursday, locally up to 8 inches, with isolated storm totals reaching 30 inches (76 cm) over Michoacán, Colima and Jalisco — life-threatening flooding and mudslides in steep terrain. No Mexico casualties or damage reports had surfaced as of Monday morning.
items.title: Oct 12: Simon weakens to Category 3 (115 mph) off Mexico; isolated 30-inch rain totals forecast

items.summary: Hurricane Isaias formed as Tropical Depression Nine in the Gulf on Oct 6, was named Oct 7, and became the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season on Oct 8 (80 mph) — one of the latest first hurricanes in Atlantic history (record: Oct 8, 1905). It peaked at Category 3 with 120 mph winds on Oct 9, then made landfall near Destin, Florida around 8:30 PM CT Friday, Oct 9 as a Category 2 with 105 mph winds. It was downgraded by 4 a.m. CT Saturday and became post-tropical over Alabama later Oct 10.
items.title: Oct 9: Hurricane Isaias makes landfall near Destin, FL as Category 2 (105 mph) after peaking at Cat 3

items.summary: Four deaths are confirmed: 2 in Escambia County, Florida and 2 in Alabama (Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey confirmed the two Alabama deaths Oct 10) — three killed by falling trees and one by generator carbon-monoxide poisoning, per NPR on Oct 12. Peak power outages reached roughly 940,000 customer accounts (over 1 million at one point per FoxWeather). As of Monday morning Oct 12, about 30% of Florida Panhandle customers were still without power (down from the peak), under 1% in Alabama; about 428,000 were still out in Florida at the last FoxWeather update (Oct 11). Pensacola was under a boil-water notice (Emerald Coast Utilities Authority).
items.title: Isaias toll: 4 dead; ~940k peak outages, ~30% of Panhandle still out Monday morning

items.summary: Gov. Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency for 25 Florida counties on Oct 8; Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey declared for 40 counties. Mandatory evacuations of coastal Okaloosa County, Florida began at noon Thursday Oct 8; three Okaloosa airports closed Thursday evening; an evacuation notice went out for the western portion of Dauphin Island, Alabama.
items.title: Oct 8: states of emergency in 25 FL and 40 AL counties; coastal evacuations and airport closures

items.source_name: WNCY (BSEE data via Earth Science Associates)
items.summary: Pre-landfall on Oct 8, personnel were evacuated from 121 Gulf production platforms and 5 non-dynamic rigs; 63% of Gulf oil production (1.3 million bpd) and 57% of natural gas production (1.1 Bcf/d) were shut in, with roughly 9 million barrels of oil potentially lost over the storm's duration. The most exposed operators: BP, Chevron, ENI, Murphy Oil and Shell.
items.title: Oct 8: 63% of Gulf oil output (1.3M bpd) shut in; 121 platforms evacuated ahead of Isaias

items.summary: Isaias's inland remnants spawned confirmed tornadoes: the NWS confirmed an EF0 near East Arcadia, Bladen County, NC (~12:54 PM EDT Oct 11, 1.68-mile path, 75 mph peak, no injuries), three tornadoes in Georgia on Oct 10 (EF0 near Captolo and an EF1 at 105 mph near Newington), and a small tornado in Wallace, NC on Oct 11 that damaged a church and power lines with no injuries. Western North Carolina saw flooding plus an 840,000-gallon sewage spill into Hunting Creek, Burke County on Oct 11. NC Gov. Josh Stein said Monday that no one was reported hurt in the weekend storms. Separately, remnants of Pacific storm Rachel brought heavy rain and dangerous surf to Southern California (homes damaged in Long Beach, Newport Beach streets flooded) and one of Las Vegas's wettest October days.
items.title: Oct 10-11: Isaias remnants spawn tornadoes in NC and GA; 840k-gallon NC sewage spill; Rachel floods SoCal

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (5 AM PDT outlook)
items.summary: The NHC's 8 a.m. EDT Monday tropical weather outlook showed no active tropical cyclones in the Atlantic basin. One disturbance — an elongated low a few hundred miles west of the Cabo Verde Islands — carries a low 20% formation chance through both 48 hours and 7 days, with heavy rain and flooding risk for the western Cabo Verde Islands. NHC was also monitoring two tropical waves; the next Atlantic name would be Josephine.
items.title: Oct 12: no active Atlantic cyclones; one Cabo Verde disturbance at 20% formation chance

items.event_time_ist: 8 a.m. MDT advisory, Oct 12 (1400 GMT); CNN update ~12:30 PM PDT, Oct 12
items.summary: Hurricane Simon continued weakening Monday: CNN (~12:30 PM PDT) reports 105 mph per the latest NHC update; the 8 a.m. MDT NHC advisory had 110 mph with the center ~55 mi west-southwest of Cabo Corrientes, moving northwest at just 3 mph. CNN reports landfall now expected sometime Thursday with winds near 100 mph; an AccuWeather expert says Simon could ultimately stall and never make a true landfall as an organized storm. The hurricane warning (Playa Perula to El Roblito plus Las Islas Marias) remains in effect.
items.title: Hurricane Simon downgraded to Category 2 as it crawls off Mexico's Pacific coast

items.event_time_ist: Announced at a news conference, Oct 12
items.summary: First reported Mexico casualty from Simon: an elderly person died in the southwestern state of Guerrero, according to Mexico's national Civil Protection coordinator during a news conference with President Claudia Sheinbaum. Sheinbaum described overall damage from Simon as 'minor,' saying Guerrero saw the most damage though less than expected, with some damage in Colima; she noted that Tropical Storm Rachel's impacts in Baja California were greater.
items.title: First reported Mexico death from Simon: elderly person in Guerrero

items.event_time_ist: Closures in effect since 6 p.m. local time, Oct 10
items.summary: Both of Mexico's main Pacific tourist airports are shut: Puerto Vallarta International will stay closed until 8 a.m. local time Tuesday, Oct 13 (extended, per Pacific Airport Group), and Manzanillo's airport has suspended all commercial flights — airlines canceled every scheduled flight over the storm threat, per GAP aviation notices. Both airports stopped operating at 6 p.m. local time Oct 10. Mexico's navy has also closed navigation at ports including Puerto Vallarta and Manzanillo.
items.title: Manzanillo airport flights suspended; Puerto Vallarta closure extended to Tuesday morning

items.event_time_ist: Overnight into Sunday, Oct 11
items.summary: Simon's slow crawl brought flooding to Manzanillo, Mexico's largest Pacific port: heavy rain flooded homes and streets overnight into Sunday, with soldiers and the National Guard deployed to assist families — residents in the Alameda neighborhood waded through shin-deep water while troops bucketed water from homes. Mexico's civil protection agency kept 28 municipalities in Jalisco and Colima at its highest cyclone alert level and another 93 at high alert.
items.title: Heavy rain floods homes and streets in Manzanillo; soldiers assist residents

items.event_time_ist: Forecast period: Tuesday-Wednesday, Oct 13-14
items.summary: Simon's remnant moisture is headed for the U.S.: the Weather Prediction Center has outlined an excessive-rainfall risk across parts of the Southern High Plains and Southwest Texas on Wednesday, Oct 14, with 1-2 inches of rain and isolated totals over 3 inches; NWS offices in Lubbock and Amarillo note heavy-rain potential even after the system dissipates. A slight risk of excessive rainfall extends from New Mexico and Texas to Missouri, and a cold front interacting with the remnants brings a Level 2-out-of-5 severe weather threat (hail, tornadoes) to the Texas and Oklahoma panhandles on Tuesday.
items.title: Simon's remnant moisture to fuel heavy rain and flooding across Texas and the Plains midweek

items.event_time_ist: Morning, Oct 12
items.source_name: Newsmax / Pensacola News Journal / USA Today
items.summary: Recovery is advancing in Isaias's landfall zone: Destin Mayor Bobby Wagner told Newsmax Monday that ~80% of power is restored in Destin with 100% of water service back, and streets should be cleared of debris today. Florida Power & Light says most affected customers should have power by end of day Monday, Oct 12, with the hardest-hit parts of Escambia and Santa Rosa counties back online Tuesday, Oct 13. In Alabama, ~20,000 homes and businesses remain without power, but Alabama Power says 95% of affected customers are restored.
items.title: Isaias recovery: Destin at ~80% power and 100% water; most FL customers back by Monday night

items.event_time_ist: depression expected within 2 days of NHC outlook issued 11:00 AM PDT, Oct 12 (11:30 PM IST, Oct 12)
items.source_name: NHC Tropical Weather Outlook (via El Dorado Weather)
items.summary: NHC's Tropical Weather Outlook (11 AM PDT, Oct 12) raised the broad low-pressure system (EP93) several hundred miles south-southwest of Guatemala to a 90% formation chance through both 48 hours and 7 days (up from 80%/90% at 5 AM PDT). A tropical depression is expected to form well south of southern Mexico in the next two days while the system moves west-northwestward at around 10 mph. A 1009 mb low has formed near 08N93W with a large area of showers and thunderstorms.
items.title: New tropical depression expected to form south of southern Mexico (EP93)

items.event_time_ist: NHC Advisory 21 issued 8:00 AM PDT (8:30 PM IST), Oct 12
items.source_name: NHC Hurricane Simon Public Advisory (via Ventusky)
items.summary: NHC Advisory 21 kept Simon at 110 mph (Cat 2), ~55 mi WSW of Cabo Corrientes crawling NW at 3 mph, and Mexico downgraded coastal warnings: hurricane warning lowered to hurricane watch from north of Cabo Corrientes to El Roblito, and hurricane warning lowered to tropical storm warning from Playa Perula north to Cabo Corrientes. Remaining: hurricane warning for Las Islas Marias only; hurricane watch north of Cabo Corrientes to Bahia Tempehuaya; tropical storm warning Playa Perula to Cabo Corrientes. NHC's 16:05 UTC discussion forecasts a northeastward turn and movement inland across Sinaloa on Thursday, with additional 2-4 inches of rain (isolated 8 inches) over Colima, Jalisco, Nayarit and Sinaloa through early Thursday and isolated storm totals up to 30 inches possible over Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco — life-threatening flooding and mudslides.
items.title: Simon: coastal warnings downgraded; landfall now expected Thursday in Sinaloa

items.event_time_ist: as of Monday morning, Oct 12 (PDT)
items.summary: As of Monday morning, Oct 12, about 146,000 structures had no power in Florida (concentrated in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties) and around 20,000 in Alabama, per PowerOutage.us trackers — down from a ~950,000-customer peak (Edison Electric Institute). FPL, the hardest-hit utility (435,000 outages), now expects 85% restoration by end of Monday — a downward revision of its initial 95% estimate — with hardest-hit Escambia/Santa Rosa areas back online Tuesday, Oct 13. Alabama Power says 95% of affected customers are restored, with longer work in heavily damaged areas. Pensacola's boil-water notice remains in effect.
items.title: Isaias recovery: ~146k still without power in Florida, ~20k in Alabama; FPL trims Monday estimate

items.event_time_ist: authorized Oct 10, 2026 (Saturday)
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Energy authorized an emergency exchange of up to 4 million barrels of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve on Oct 10 — up to 2 million barrels each for ExxonMobil and BP America to keep refineries running, to be returned in 2027 with premium barrels. By Friday afternoon, about 71.5% of daily Gulf oil production (~1.46 million bpd) and 58.8% of natural gas were shut in, with 100+ platforms evacuated and 8 rigs evacuated or moved.
items.title: DOE authorized 4M-barrel SPR emergency exchange after Isaias shut in Gulf production

items.event_time_ist: NHC Advisory 22 issued 2:00 PM PDT (2:30 AM IST, Oct 13), Oct 12
items.summary: NHC Advisory 22 (2 PM MST Oct 12) lowered Simon's maximum sustained winds to 100 mph (still Category 2), centered about 75 miles W of Cabo Corrientes and about 210 miles S of Mazatlan, moving west-northwest at 3 mph with a minimum central pressure of 969 mb. Mexico discontinued the Tropical Storm Warning from Playa Perula to Cabo Corrientes; a hurricane warning remains in effect only for Las Islas Marias, with a hurricane watch from Cabo Corrientes to Bahia Tempehuaya. Forecast: near Las Islas Marias tonight into Tuesday, then approaching the west-central Mexico coast Wednesday into Thursday; NHC says Simon could re-intensify somewhat by Wednesday and remain a hurricane through midweek, with rapid weakening after it moves inland late in the week. Rainfall: 5-10 inches across coastal west-central Mexico with isolated maximums of 15 inches over Sinaloa by Thursday; a dangerous storm surge is possible along the immediate coast near Las Islas Marias.
items.title: Simon down to 100 mph in NHC Advisory 22; coastal warnings trimmed again

items.event_time_ist: Jalisco civil protection briefing held morning of Oct 12 (aired ~11:15 AM PDT / 11:45 PM IST, Oct 12)
items.source_name: Jalisco civil protection briefing (via Jalisco Noticias)
items.summary: Jalisco's civil protection briefing Monday outlined the Simon response so far: roughly 14,000 people evacuated, about 8,500 tourists kept safely in hotels, and just over 800 people remaining in shelters. Starting Tuesday, Oct 13, non-essential preventive measures are being lifted: in-person school classes resume and tourism and private-supply businesses can gradually reopen stores and shopping centers; public transit is resuming, though government administrative offices stay closed pending infrastructure evaluations. Officials reported significant storm-surge damage in Cihuatlan and La Huerta, a river overflow affecting Colima, and a pending agricultural-damage assessment in Tomatlan; no wind damage was reported, though 3-4 meter swells are still expected through Wednesday. Azteca ADN40 field reports separately put Puerto Vallarta/Nayarit affected homes above 3,000.
items.title: Jalisco briefing: ~14,000 evacuated, schools resume Tuesday Oct 13; storm surge damage in Cihuatlan/La Huerta

items.event_time_ist: 11:00 AM CDT (9:30 PM IST), Oct 12
items.title: Gulf of Mexico oil/gas shut-ins drop to ~30% as crews return
items.summary: US Gulf of Mexico producers had shut in 29.63% of current daily oil production and 24.81% of natural gas production as of 11:00 a.m. CDT Monday Oct 12, per the Marine Minerals Administration - a sharp recovery from Friday's 71.5% oil / 58.8% gas peak ahead of Isaias's landfall. Personnel remain evacuated from only 5 of 371 manned platforms and 1 of 11 fixed rigs as operators inspect facilities and restart output.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 11, 2026 (exact time unknown)
items.title: Landslide destroys house in Acapulco amid Simon's heavy rains
items.summary: Heavy rains ahead of Hurricane Simon triggered a landslide in Acapulco, Guerrero that destroyed a house, per AFP. The damage occurred as Simon's outer rainbands soaked Mexico's Pacific coast over the weekend. It is separate from the previously reported Guerrero storm death (an elderly person).

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (early-morning PDT report; flooding overnight Oct 11-12)
items.summary: Reuters on-the-ground reporting Oct 12: rising water levels in the Marabasco River in Cihuatlan, Jalisco (near the Colima border) prompted patrols by the Mexican Army, Civil Protection officials and the Red Cross; floodwater inundated streets and low-lying areas of the town overnight and riverside communities were placed on alert for possible evacuations. In the port city of Manzanillo, Colima, residents waded through flooded homes and streets as navy personnel helped remove water - resident Maria Elena Vazquez said 'Everything got flooded,' with water at ankle level inside homes. Corroborated by Rapid Times NGR (same wire reporting) and Virgin Radio Dubai/AFP (Sunday flooding in Manzanillo). Separately, Fox Weather projects Simon could make landfall near Mazatlan on Wednesday night, earlier than the NHC's Thursday Sinaloa window - a single-outlet forecast, not an official call.
items.title: Simon flooding: Marabasco River rising prompts Army/Red Cross patrols in Cihuatlan; riverside communities on evacuation alert

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (afternoon local briefing; 2:45 PM local outage counts)
items.title: FPL cuts Monday restoration target to 70% in Escambia/Santa Rosa after 'extensive damage' found
items.summary: FPL President/CEO Scott Bores announced in a Monday operational briefing that Monday-night restoration estimates for Escambia and Santa Rosa counties were lowered to 70% of customers able to safely accept power, down from the earlier 85% (originally 95%) target, after crews reached previously inaccessible communities and found severe tree damage and 700+ power poles snapped by falling timber. FPL showed 55,290 customers without power in Escambia and 34,790 in Santa Rosa at 2:45 Monday afternoon. Remaining customers to be reconnected Tuesday; company-wide 75%+ restored (~330,000 accounts), aiming for 85% overall Monday night. Bores blamed Hurricane Isaias's destructive western eyewall cutting directly over the two counties. 17,000 workers deployed 24/7; 15 customer relief sites handing out ice/water.

items.event_time_ist: Weekend of Oct 10-11, 2026 (reported Monday, Oct 12, 2026)
items.title: Tropical Storm Rachel's aftermath: deaths and missing persons in Baja California
items.summary: Baja California Gov. Marina del Pilar said at least 10 people were reported missing and a young girl dead in the aftermath of Tropical Storm Rachel, with more than 50 people in temporary shelters (AP wire). A second outlet, GG North, reports flooding near Ensenada left 1 dead and 7 missing, a partial evacuation of Ensenada's IMSS Bienestar General Hospital (water leaks and electrical failures), more than 4,000 emergency reports and 200+ rescues statewide, and school suspensions Monday. Figures vary between outlets as the situation develops. Earlier in this watch, President Sheinbaum had already noted Rachel's impacts in Baja California were greater than Simon's on the mainland.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 11, 2026 ~9:00 PM IST (Sunday ~8:30 AM PDT)
items.title: Man dies after being pulled from Rachel-fueled surf at Dockweiler Beach, Los Angeles
items.summary: A man was pulled unconscious from the ocean near Tower 42 at Dockweiler Beach, Playa del Rey, on Sunday morning and pronounced dead after about 20 minutes of resuscitation efforts, per Surfer citing KTLA. Police found no indication of foul play. The death was initially reported as a drowning, but the LA County Medical Examiner will determine the official cause; the lifeguard specialist noted a medical emergency was also possible. The incident came amid a High Surf Advisory (5-8 ft breaking waves, powerful rip currents) driven partly by former Hurricane Rachel, plus severe coastal flooding across Southern California.

items.event_time_ist: 3:00 AM IST, Oct 13 (4:30 PM CT, Oct 12)
items.summary: Florida Power & Light had restored power to 168,510 customers in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties, with 81,220 still without power, as of 4:30 p.m. CT Monday (Pensacola News Journal, updated <1h before this report). FPL still targets 70% of homes restored by Monday night — including all schools and critical infrastructure — and the remainder by end of Tuesday; the FPL app has falsely shown some customers as restored.
items.title: Isaias outage update: 81,220 still without power in Escambia/Santa Rosa as of Monday 4:30 p.m. CT

items.event_time_ist: Monday afternoon, Oct 12 (PT)
items.summary: Long Beach Mayor Rex Richardson confirmed Monday afternoon that eight buildings (13 residences) on the Alamitos Peninsula remain red-tagged as unsafe and one building yellow-tagged after post-tropical Rachel's surf waves battered the waterfront; no additional buildings were tagged but damage continues to worsen. Mandatory evacuation orders stand for the Seaside Walk 6400/6500 blocks; broader Peninsula advisories have been lifted, and NWS coastal flood warnings were downgraded to an advisory through 2 p.m. Tuesday. (Confirmed by MyNewsLA; ABC7 also carried the 13-red-tagged count.)
items.title: Post-tropical Rachel: 8 buildings (13 homes) red-tagged on Long Beach Peninsula; damage still worsening

items.event_time_ist: Sun, Oct 11, 2026 (pronounced dead ~12:21 PM ET, ~9:51 PM IST)
items.summary: Greenwood County Coroner's Office: 67-year-old Christopher John Miller died Sunday Oct 11 at his home at 6802 Highway 702, Ninety Six, S.C., after a large tree collapsed onto the house during the remnants of Hurricane Isaias; pronounced dead at 12:21 p.m.; cause of death blunt force trauma; manner ruled accidental. Isaias's U.S. death toll rises to 5 (2 Florida, 2 Alabama, 1 South Carolina).
items.title: Fifth Isaias death confirmed: South Carolina man killed by fallen tree

items.event_time_ist: Weekend of Oct 10-11, 2026 (reported Mon, Oct 12, 2026)
items.summary: Following the weekend rainfall from the remnants of Isaias, Buncombe County (Asheville, NC) reported the discharge of ~12,000 gallons of untreated wastewater into the French Broad River. Small relative to the 840,000-gallon Burke County spill already reported.
items.title: Buncombe County reports 12,000-gallon wastewater spill into French Broad River after Isaias weekend rain

items.event_time_ist: Night of Oct 12 into Oct 13, 2026 (expected formation window, local Pacific)
items.source_name: NHC (Tropical Weather Outlook, 5 PM PDT Oct 12)
items.summary: NHC's 5 PM PDT Oct 12 Tropical Weather Outlook raises EP93 - a broad low pressure several hundred miles south-southwest of Guatemala's coast - to near 100% formation chance through both 48 hours and 7 days. Showers and thunderstorms are beginning to show signs of organization; a tropical depression or tropical storm is expected to form well south of southern Mexico later tonight or tomorrow, moving west-northwest at ~10 mph.
items.title: EP93 at near-100% formation chance - NHC expects tropical depression or storm tonight or tomorrow

items.event_time_ist: Night of Saturday, Oct 10 (dive) / Sunday morning, Oct 11, 2026 (body recovered) - Mazatlan local time
items.summary: Juan 'Patines' (aka Juanito/El Chicali), a well-known cliff diver at Mazatlan's Glorieta Rodolfo Sanchez Taboada ('El Clavadista'), died Saturday night, Oct 10, after jumping into Simon-driven surf with waves up to 3 meters and being unable to reach the rocks. A fellow diver tried to save him but the swell defeated the rescue; municipal aquatic rescue teams resumed the search at 5 a.m. Sunday, Oct 11, and found his body near the same spot. Official identity still uncertain across outlets (some say Juan 'N' ~50, others Ricardo 'N' 35).
items.title: Mazatlan cliff diver 'Juan Patines' killed by Simon surf; body recovered Sunday

items.event_time_ist: Forecast for around midnight Thursday, Oct 15, 2026 (Mazatlan local time)
items.summary: Mexico's SMN coordinator Fabian Vazquez, speaking at the presidential press conference, said the forecast takes Simon northward while gradually weakening, with effects beginning around Wednesday and the closest approach/impact expected very near Mazatlan, Sinaloa, around midnight Thursday, Oct 15 - still a forecast, not confirmed. Consistent with NHC's Wed-Thu approach to Mexico's west-central coast.
items.title: Mexico's SMN: Simon expected near Mazatlan around midnight Thursday, Oct 15
2026 breaks the Northeast Pacific's all-time ACE record
items.summary: The 2026 northeastern Pacific hurricane season set the basin's all-time record for Accumulated Cyclone Energy: 318.8 as of 5:00 PM EDT Sunday Oct 11 (per Colorado State University data), beating the 318.1 record from 2018. Hurricane Simon pushed the season over the top. Season to date: 21 storms, 11 hurricanes (all but two major), three Category 5s (Genevieve, Lowell, Polo - Polo the basin's second-most intense by pressure), 10 storms affecting land. Hawaii took the brunt with one of its worst hurricane seasons (Lala, Moke, Lowell, Nolo). Driven by a record-setting El Nino; meanwhile Atlantic ACE is under 20% of normal - Hurricane Isaias was the Atlantic's latest first hurricane on record.

items.event_time_ist: Date uncertain — reported by officials Monday, Oct 12 (wall collapsed during Simon's weekend rains)
items.title: Additional Hurricane Simon fatality in Mexico identified: Albino Moreno Jimenez, 71
items.summary: Guerrero governor Evelyn Salgado's Monday briefing confirmed the Simon death was 71-year-old Albino Moreno Jimenez, killed when a retaining wall collapsed on him in the western outskirts of Chilpancingo, Guerrero while he was feeding his animals. The detail traces to Guerrero-based news agency IRZA. Simon death toll in Mexico stands at 2 (this victim plus the Mazatlan cliff diver 'Juan Patines' killed by Simon surf Oct 10, already on the feed; plus 1 Rachel death in Baja California, also already reported).

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026, Monday (DeSantis press conference; exact time not stated)
items.title: DeSantis Monday briefing: ~400 FL State Guard soldiers deployed for Isaias recovery; $10M zero-interest business loans; Walmart $1M
items.summary: Gov. DeSantis' Monday press conference: Florida State Guard deployed nearly 400 soldiers (1,700 miles of roadway cleared; 4,000 cases of water, 1,700 meals, 2,600 bags of ice, 2,200 tarps distributed; 20+ flight hours on search/rescue and damage assessment). FloridaCommerce made $10M available in short-term, zero-interest loans for impacted businesses; Walmart committed $1M in funding and supplies for Panhandle recovery; the state insurance assistance hub opened Monday. DeSantis said 'more than 70% of the accounts have been restored' and that 'probably about 500,000' accounts lost power at one point or another.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026, Monday (announced; exact time not stated)
items.title: Mexico's Navy (Semar) closed Pacific ports across Sinaloa, Nayarit, Jalisco and Michoacan to navigation ahead of Simon
items.summary: Semar announced preventive navigation closures Monday ahead of Cat-2 Simon's Wednesday-Thursday approach to Mexico's west-central coast. Minor vessels: Topolobampo and Teacapan (Sinaloa); San Blas, La Cruz de Huanacaxtle, Nuevo Vallarta, Chacala (Nayarit); Puerto Vallarta and Barra de Navidad (Jalisco); Lazaro Cardenas (Michoacan). Major vessels: San Blas (Nayarit) and Puerto Vallarta (Jalisco). Sinaloa port closures are new (PVR/Manzanillo were already shut Sunday). Conagua flagged high surf, landslide, river-overflow and flooding risk across the watch zone.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (reported Oct 12; exact rescue time undetermined)
items.summary: Mexico's Defense Secretariat (Defensa) airlifted 32 people (9 men, 10 women, 13 children) and 3 dogs from Rancho Genesis in Ensenada, Baja California, after Tropical Storm Rachel's rains cut all ground access. The evacuation took 5 helicopter flights plus an initial reconnaissance flight; Baja California Gov. Marina del Pilar arranged the federal air support through President Sheinbaum. Baja casualty figures unchanged (1 girl dead, 10 missing, 50+ in shelters). CNPC reported saldo blanco (no fatalities, no major damage) in Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco from Simon.
items.title: Tropical Storm Rachel aftermath: 32 people + 3 dogs airlifted from flooded Rancho Genesis, Ensenada

items.event_time_ist: Monday afternoon, Oct 12, 2026 (San Blas, Nayarit local time)
items.summary: Seawater flooding was reported Monday afternoon in at least three neighborhoods of San Blas, Nayarit — including Benito Juárez — with some residents moving to shelters. It is the first verified neighborhood-level flood impact from Hurricane Simon in Nayarit, which remains under a hurricane watch; Puerto Vallarta's earlier Monday conditions were described as less severe than feared.
items.title: Seawater flooding hits San Blas, Nayarit; residents moved to shelters

items.event_time_ist: Planned 12:01 AM Tue, Oct 13, 2026 (Puerto Vallarta local time)
items.summary: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacífico (GAP) announced a planned resumption of commercial operations at Puerto Vallarta airport at 12:01 a.m. Tuesday, Oct 13 (per La Jornada, via Drive Mexico Magazine's Monday evening report). Caveat: GAP's official Oct 11 NOTAM-based notice said the airport would stay closed until 8:00 a.m. local Tue Oct 13 — the two announced times conflict, so treat the reopening time as unconfirmed until GAP's official channels confirm. Ports at Puerto Vallarta and San Blas remained closed to navigation Monday evening.
items.title: GAP plans Puerto Vallarta airport reopening 12:01 AM Tue — earlier than official 8 AM notice

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (bodies recovered Monday; reported Monday evening)
items.summary: Baja California's prosecutor now reports 4 dead in the Maneadero area of Ensenada from post-tropical Rachel — including 4-year-old Aarón (body found Monday at Rancho Richi), Silvia (30), and Ivón (35); two of the dead are minors. Five people remain missing (Rosa María, 42; Luis Fernando, 17; Rosalinda, 23; Leonel, 10; Gael Gustavo, 14), and authorities say they have no unified missing-person count. Also: 8 patients evacuated from flooded Ensenada General Hospital; ~25 neighborhoods without power; ~10 wooden homes swept away at Rancho Génesis and Rancho Abierto; 30 families evacuated in San Francisquito; 182 people in shelters. Previous toll was 1 girl dead, 10 missing.
items.title: Rachel's Baja toll rises: 4 dead, 5 missing in Ensenada

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (8:00 PM MST advisory; issued ~8:00 PM PDT, Oct 12)
items.summary: NHC Hurricane Simon Advisory 23 (8 PM MST Oct 12): winds hold at 100 mph (Cat 2), 969 mb, ~85 mi W of Cabo Corrientes, drifting WNW at 3 mph. Watch change: Mexico replaced the Hurricane Watch from Cabo Corrientes to Escuinapa with a Tropical Storm Watch; Hurricane Warning remains for Las Islas Marías and Hurricane Watch north of Escuinapa to Bahía Tempehuaya. Correction to the 8:25 PM note, which said there were no watch changes. Gradual re-intensification possible to ~85 kt by 72-96h; track confidence low (near-stationary possible).
items.title: Simon Advisory 23: hurricane watch segment downgraded to tropical storm watch

items.summary: Royal Caribbean's Voyager of the Seas cut its Puerto Vallarta port call due to Hurricane Simon and instead visited Cabo San Lucas a second time, staying well clear of the storm's forecast track off the west-central Mexico coast. The sailing's return to Los Angeles on Friday, Oct 16, is unchanged, with refundable amounts reimbursed at sailing's end. The ship would otherwise have had to sail through the forecast track heading back north.
items.title: Voyager of the Seas drops Puerto Vallarta call for Simon

items.event_time_ist: Monday, Oct 12, 2026 (AFP Monday wire)
items.title: Simon flooding and landslides hit riverside communities in Michoacán and Colima
items.summary: AFP Monday wrap: flooding and landslides had already hit communities close to rivers and streams in Michoacán and Colima. Simon weakened to Cat 2, did not make landfall, and was moving away from the coast; a rain alert remains in place and officials warn waves up to 5 meters high are still expected in some coastal areas. CNPC's latest: Simon will hit Mazatlán, Sinaloa as a Category 1 hurricane; Puerto Vallarta awoke to clear skies Monday. Five-death toll unchanged (1 Simon/Guerrero, 4 Rachel/Baja).

items.event_time_ist: as of Monday AM, Oct 12, 2026
items.title: Florida co-ops: ~36,000 members out Monday AM; CHELCO's largest storm response ever
items.summary: NRECA/electric.coop (updated 11 a.m. ET Mon): ~36,000 Florida co-op members still out early Monday, most of them ~20,000 in CHELCO's coastal areas; CHELCO CEO expects nearly all members back by Tuesday evening (~96h after landfall), calling it 'the largest storm response in CHELCO's history'; 15 of 16 CHELCO substations reenergized. 250,000 co-op members in the dark at peak across FL/GA/AL/MS. Alabama co-ops: ~8,000 members out Monday AM (down from 103,000 peak); Baldwin EMC fully restored Sunday.

items.event_time_ist: Oct 13, 2026 (announced Oct 12, 2026)
items.summary: Veteran-led nonprofit Team Rubicon stood up its first Hurricane Isaias disaster relief operation: up to 30 Greyshirts per day from Tue Oct 13 in Milton and across Santa Rosa County for debris management, roof tarping, heavy equipment and sawyer work. Its route-clearance team removed 54 obstructions over the weekend and cut paths for power crews across Santa Rosa County; op runs through at least Oct 21, with a Pensacola op expected soon.
items.title: Team Rubicon launches Isaias relief operation in Santa Rosa County

items.event_time_ist: 10:00 PM CDT, Oct 12
items.summary: FPL announced Monday night it met its revised restoration target: more than 380,000 outages restored as of 10 p.m. CDT (85%+ of the 435,000 customers impacted by Hurricane Isaias), restoration essentially complete in 6 of 8 counties, and all critical infrastructure facilities plus schools scheduled to open Tuesday restored. Crews remain on track to essentially complete restoration in the hardest-hit Escambia and Santa Rosa counties by end of day Tuesday. ~17,000 restoration workers deployed from 29 states; 480+ drone/helicopter damage-assessment flights. 10+ customer outage relief stations open (ice, water, restoration answers). Single-sourced (FPL's own release; corroboration search surfaced only FPL's own newsroom - PNJ's latest figures are 4:30 PM Monday and consistent with the trajectory).
items.title: FPL: >85% of Isaias customers restored Monday night (380,000+), 6 of 8 counties essentially complete

items.event_time_ist: 10:48 PM PDT, Oct 12
items.summary: NHC Intermediate Advisory 23A (~10:48 PM PDT): Hurricane Simon holds at Category 2, 100 mph, but central pressure rose to 977 mb (from 969 mb in Advisory 23) - a weakening trend; ~90 mi W of Cabo Corrientes, now moving NW at 3 mph. No new watches/warnings: hurricane warning Las Islas Marias; tropical storm watch Cabo Corrientes to Escuinapa; hurricane watch Escuinapa to Bahia Tempehuaya. Forecast: 80 mph Tuesday, re-intensifying to ~100 mph Thu-Fri near the west-central Mexico coast, post-tropical by Saturday. Mexico SMN's 21:00 CDT bulletin (verified via CONAGUA/CNPC posts) is consistent: Cat 2, 155 km/h (96 mph), 135 km W of Cabo Corrientes, 315 km S of Mazatlan, WNW 6 km/h; heavy to very heavy rain for western Jalisco, coastal Nayarit, southern Sinaloa.
items.title: Simon Advisory 23A: still Cat 2 (100 mph), pressure up to 977 mb; moving NW

items.event_time_ist: 10:31 PM PDT, Oct 12
items.summary: TV Azteca Sinaloa documented heavy rain falling in Mazatlan Monday night as Simon's outer effects arrive ahead of the forecast Wed-Thu coastal approach (on-screen: 'LLUVIAS POR SIMON' / 'Comienzan las primeras lluvias en Mazatlan por el huracan Simon'). First verified on-the-ground weather impact in Mazatlan from this storm. Image: reused verified Simon satellite photo (image-search results for Mazatlan rain were unusable: unrelated/2018-Hurricane-Willa or wrong-storm images).
items.title: First Simon-linked rains begin in Mazatlan (TV Azteca Sinaloa)

items.event_time_ist: 11:30 AM IST, Oct 13
items.summary: NHC Public Advisory 23A (11:00 PM MST / 11:00 PM PDT Mon Oct 12): Simon weakened to Category 1 with max sustained winds of 90 mph, down from 100 mph (Cat 2) in Advisory 23 at 8 PM MST. Center at 20.5N 107.1W, moving NW at 3 mph, pressure 977 mb. Flooding rains continue along the west-central Mexico coast.
items.title: Hurricane Simon weakens to Category 1 (90 mph) off Mexico

items.event_time_ist: 11:30 AM IST, Oct 13
items.summary: NHC Tropical Weather Outlook 11 PM PDT Mon Oct 12: Invest EP93 south of southern Mexico shows improved signs of organization with increased shower/thunderstorm activity; formation chance remains near 100% (48h and 7d). A tropical depression or tropical storm is expected to form well south of southern Mexico within the next day or so, moving WNW ~10 mph. Still unnamed (next name: Trudy); NHC advises southwestern Mexico interests to keep monitoring.
items.title: EP93 (future Trudy) organizes south of Mexico; formation expected within a day or so

items.event_time_ist: Monday Oct 12 (announced at the presidential morning presser, Oct 12)
items.source_name: CentralND / Meridiano Colima (via Monday mañanera presser)
items.summary: Colima Gov. Indira Vizcaino Silva told President Sheinbaum at Monday's morning presser that Simon's weekend rains caused flooding and landslides affecting 71 homes and 35 businesses, plus roads, schools and medical units across Colima — though the track change spared the state a direct hit. Saldo blanco: zero deaths, injuries or missing in the state; 177 people housed in 10 temporary shelters. SMN rainfall totals: up to 500 mm regionally, 272 mm in Colima, 155 mm in Manzanillo; CFE power 100% restored. The state also logged 73 fallen trees, 67 flood spots, 6 landslides and 11 school buildings damaged (9 in Manzanillo).
items.title: Colima damage tally: 71 homes, 35 businesses damaged by Simon rains; no casualties

items.event_time_ist: Sunday night, Oct 11 (announced); Monday Oct 12 (in effect)
items.summary: Interim Gov. Graciela Dominguez Nava suspended classes for both shifts Monday Oct 12 in seven southern Sinaloa municipalities — Mazatlan, Escuinapa, Rosario, Concordia, Cosala, Elota and San Ignacio — as Simon approached; the Autonomous University of Sinaloa (UAS) suspended its campuses in the same seven. Separately Monday: Nayarit suspended classes in 12 municipalities, Colima in 4 (Manzanillo, Tecoman, Armeria, Minatitlan, morning shift), and Baja California statewide under Rachel; Jalisco reopens schools Tuesday Oct 13.
items.title: Sinaloa suspended classes in 7 southern municipalities Monday ahead of Simon

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (announcement date; exact time unknown)
items.title: Florida opens interest-free disaster recovery loans for farmers hit by Isaias
items.summary: Florida Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson announced (Oct 12) interest-free loans of up to $500,000 for farmers, ranchers and aquaculture producers with Hurricane Isaias damage in 30 Florida counties (incl. Escambia, Santa Rosa, Okaloosa), covering fences, equipment, greenhouses, buildings, debris removal and aquaculture restocking. Producers urged to photograph damage and save receipts. Program sits in a revolving state loan fund ($75M from 2023 special session + $40M more in 2025).

items.event_time_ist: Oct 9-11, 2026 (first reported Oct 9; surfaced in this watch's sweeps now)
items.source_name: Contra Linea / Latinus (via Wikipedia), corroborated by AP/CNN
items.summary: First concrete Guerrero damage figures in this watch from Simon's weekend pass: ~65,780 customers lost electricity across Guerrero (Contra Linea, Oct 9); in Acapulco, 150 power poles downed, 20 houses flooded, 2 people injured (Latinus, Oct 9), and the Puerto Marques electrical substation was flooded and shut down. AP/CNN corroborate that federal authorities were working to restore power in Acapulco. Chilpancingo toll unchanged at 1 (Albino Moreno Jimenez, 71, wall collapse).
items.title: Simon weekend damage figures surface for Guerrero/Acapulco: ~65,780 customers out, 150 poles downed, 2 injured

items.event_time_ist: Oct 12, 2026 (AP update, surfaced in this watch's sweeps now)
items.summary: New details on Rachel's Baja toll (Ensenada): the four recovered bodies are a 13-year-old girl (Sunday) plus two women and a 4-year-old boy (Monday); six remain missing - four in Ensenada and a father-son fishing pair from San Felipe who did not return Saturday. The 32 people rescued by military helicopter at the Ensenada ranch included 22 foreigners - Germans and Americans, some missionaries; 13 of the 32 were youths. ~14,000 federal and state personnel deployed across Baja California. AFP confirms the four recovered bodies and the helicopter rescues.
items.title: Baja toll refined: four bodies identified in Ensenada, 22 foreigners among 32 helicopter rescues, 14,000 personnel deployed

items.event_time_ist: Guerrero Civil Protection assessment cutoff: 6 PM CST, Oct 12, 2026 (= 5:30 AM IST, Oct 13, 2026); published in press Oct 13, 2026
items.title: Simon damage tally rises: 201 homes in 21 Guerrero municipalities; Acapulco rainfall record
items.summary: Guerrero Civil Protection's latest assessment raises Simon's toll to 201 damaged homes across 21 municipalities (6 fully collapsed, 182 flooded, 13 more with landslide or structural damage), up from 112 in 20 municipalities. Acapulco is the hardest-hit municipality (2 injured, 20 homes flooded, 150 businesses waterlogged, 60 vehicles stranded) and set an all-time rainfall record at 391 mm, with up to 500 mm suspected. Mexico's SMN forecasts Simon degrading to Category 1 Tuesday-Wednesday and making landfall in Sinaloa around midnight Thursday, Oct 15, with direct effects on Mazatlan at lower intensity (~160 km/h gusts). Simon's death toll remains 2 (Chilpancingo wall-collapse victim + Mazatlan cliff diver).

items.event_time_ist: Expected later today, Tue Oct 13 (5 AM PDT TWOEP issued 5:30 PM IST)
items.summary: NHC Tropical Weather Outlook 5 AM PDT Tue Oct 13: Invest EP93 south of southern Mexico has showers and thunderstorms becoming better organized with a better-defined circulation; formation chance remains high near 100% (48h and 7d). If trends continue, NHC says advisories are likely to be initiated later today on a tropical depression or tropical storm, moving generally WNW around 10 mph. The system is NOT yet classified - still no tropical depression and no Tropical Storm Trudy.
items.title: NHC: EP93 likely to get tropical-cyclone advisories 'later today' - still unnamed (next name Trudy)

items.event_time_ist: Tue Oct 13 (8 AM EDT TWOAT issued 5:30 PM IST)
items.summary: NHC Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook 8 AM EDT Tue Oct 13: the low-pressure trough a few hundred miles west-northwest of the Cabo Verde Islands is no longer expected to develop as it moves slowly north into strong upper-level winds; formation chance now low, near 0 percent for both 48 hours and 7 days. No tropical cyclones are active in the Atlantic. The only Atlantic formation watch item in this watch drops out.
items.title: Atlantic Cabo Verde disturbance fizzles out - formation chance now near 0%

items.event_time_ist: Issued 5:00 AM PDT, Oct 13 (5:30 PM IST, Oct 13)
items.title: NHC: advisories likely initiated later today on EP93 as a tropical depression or tropical storm
items.summary: NHC 5:00 AM PDT Tropical Weather Outlook (Pacific): EP93 — a broad low several hundred miles south of southern Mexico — now shows better-organized showers/thunderstorms and satellite-derived wind data indicating the circulation is becoming better defined. Formation chance remains high, near 100% (48h and 7d). NHC says if current trends continue, advisories will likely be initiated later today on a tropical depression or tropical storm; the system moves WNW ~10 mph and southwestern Mexico interests should keep monitoring. Still unnamed — the next eastern Pacific name is Trudy.
items.source_name: NWS National Hurricane Center (Tropical Weather Outlook, 5 AM PDT Oct 13)
